about: Zimmet Law Group works from Madison Avenue and publishes thirty people with a rank beside every name, from managing partner through partners, senior attorneys and associates to of counsel. That is the fullest roster in this ranking, and seven bar association memberships on its own bios is the most of any firm here.

799 reviews at 4.9, the largest count in this market. It names all four routes through a divorce, mediation, collaborative divorce, litigation and an uncontested filing, and publishes nothing at all about what any of them costs.

json_ld_descriptions: Zimmet Law Group, P.C. is a full-service law firm that handles a wide variety of legal matters for clients in New York City and the surrounding suburbs. Focused on providing personal attention and high-caliber legal services, clients regularly turn to our firm when facing issues related to family law, estate planning and administration, real estate, commercial litigation, business law, bankruptcy, and landlord-tenant disputes. In order to accommodate prospective clients, we represent people with group legal plans and those without. Contact our firm to discuss your legal matter.

score.verdict: All 5 eligibility gates passed. Strongest pillar: C; most headroom in pillar E (0/15).

subs.label: Experience
subs.evidence: Mean 19.8 years since admission across 12 of 26 named attorneys (longest 42, shortest 1) · NYS Attorney Registration database

subs.label: Roster verifiability
subs.evidence: 12 of 26 named attorneys matched to the New York register; bar numbers published on the bios

subs.label: Accountability
subs.evidence: member of New York City Bar Association, American Bar Association, American Immigration Lawyers Association and 4 more · no professional liability cover disclosed, which is not scored here: plaintiff firms in this market do not publish it, and an absence shared by every firm separates none of them

subs.label: Fee terms published
subs.evidence: Nothing about the rate, the retainer or any other price on the 5 pages we read. The court rules guarantee a client all of it in a signed agreement before the work starts; publishing it beforehand is the firm's choice

subs.label: The case explained
subs.evidence: Explains 5 stages of a matrimonial case: child support, grounds, judgment, maintenance, settlement · names collaborative, litigation, mediation, uncontested

subs.label: Billing and the retainer disclosed
subs.evidence: Says nothing about how it bills against the retainer or what happens to the unused part, on any of the 5 pages we read

subs.label: Authentic volume
subs.evidence: 799 Google reviews · Google Business Profile via Places API. 1 listing, counts summed and rating weighted by count

subs.label: Rating quality
subs.evidence: Google rating 4.9 over 799 reviews → Bayesian 4.89 (prior 4.83 weighted as 100 reviews, from 528 scored firms) · single platform, Google only

subs.label: Review recency
subs.evidence: 5 of 5 sampled reviews are from the last 12 months (newest 2026-09-05) · a sample of five per business listing, not every review

subs.label: Complaint share
subs.evidence: 0 of 5 sampled reviews rate 1 or 2 stars · a sample, so this is the shape of the complaints rather than a count of them

subs.label: Website trust & experience
subs.evidence: CWV fail · no bar numbers on bios · no fee statement · privacy policy · disclaimer · fresh content

subs.label: Search authority
subs.evidence: DR 22 → 76th pct of 17-firm cohort (median 8) 2/3 · 588 referring domains, 59th pct 1/2 · 63 organic keywords / 195 visits·mo, 41th pct 1/2 · brand demand 0/1 (pending)

subs.label: Local presence
subs.evidence: 1 operational Google Business Profile listing · 10 or more photos, which is where the API stops counting · 5 categories, hours published, which almost every listing here has and so separates nobody · the services list, Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the Places API does not expose, and NAP consistency across citations and local-pack rank have no source here, so the rest of this sub-factor leaves the scale rather than being scored as unearned

subs.label: Content, E-E-A-T & schema
subs.evidence: JSON-LD detected 1/1 · not assessed on any firm yet, so content depth and earned media and AI citations leave the scale (4 pts)

subs.label: Free consult & fee transparency
subs.evidence: fee model not published · the rate, retainer or flat fee itself is not published
